data.name: Virbhadra
data.gender_notes: Virbhadra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Virbhadra is the fearsome form of Lord Shiva, believed to have appeared to destroy a demon. The name signifies fearlessness and is derived from the Sanskrit words 'vir' (fearless) and 'bhadra' (kind or prosperous). The name Virbhadra carries the meaning “Fearless, Brahma's dreadful form” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Virbhadra usually hope their child will grow to embody fearless, brahma's dreadful form and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the fearless aspect of Lord Shiva, reminding us to face our fears with courage.
data.etymology: Virbhadra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fearless, Brahma's dreadful form.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Virbhadra total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Virbhadra is a central figure in Hindu mythology, revered particularly in the Himachal Pradesh region of India. He is depicted as a fierce warrior god with multiple arms, holding weapons, and a fiery_{(aj_)_} appearance. The Shaivite tradition invokes Virbhadra during rituals to invoke the destructive power of Lord Shiva. There are numerous temples dedicated to Virbhadra, situated in beautiful mountainous regions, where he is worshipped with great devotion and fervor.
data.spiritual_significance: Virbhadra represents the aspect of Lord Shiva that embodies fearlessness and destruction of evil. He is a reminder to believers that fearlessness is a crucial trait to possess, especially when battling inner demons or facing external adversities. Furthermore, he symbolizes the divine power to eliminate negativity and restore balance and harmony in the universe. Worship of Virbhadra is thought to provide protection against fear, anger, and negative energies.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Virbhadra symbolizes fearlessness and invincibility. The name derives from the Sanskrit words 'Vir' (hero) and 'Bhadra' (auspicious). In Hindu mythology, Virbhadra is an incarnation of Lord Shiva, embodying his fierce and protective aspects.

vedic_reference.note: Virbhadra is the name of a king in the Mahabharata who was a powerful warrior and the father of Bhishma Pitamaha. He was a descendant of the lunar dynasty and ruled over the kingdom of Hastinapur. Virbhadra is also known as Vibhishana and is considered to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
